title: Polyphia - Wikipedia
notes: American rock band from Plano, Texas, formed 2010; members Tim Henson, Scott LePage (guitars), Clay Gober (bass, 2012-), Clay Aeschliman (drums, 2016-); past drummers Brandon Burkhalter (2010-2014, 2015-2016) and Randy Methe (2014-2015). New Levels New Devils (2018) their first album to chart; Remember That You Will Die (October 2022) "further exploring trap percussion and hip hop stylings". Aeschliman endorsed by Tama and Meinl. Live at the Factory in Deep Ellum (2023); Be Not Afraid announced for 23 October 2026.

title: Remember That You Will Die - Wikipedia
notes: Released 28 October 2022 on Rise Records. Track list: Genesis, Playing God, The Audacity, Reverie, ABC, Memento Mori, Fuck Around and Find Out, All Falls Apart, Neurotica, Chimera, Bloodbath, Ego Death. Personnel: Clay Aeschliman, drums; Luke Holland, additional drums (1, 6, 9, 10); drum engineering Nick Sampson, Sean Kellett, Bryce Butler.

title: On The Beat with Clay Aeschliman of Polyphia: Talks Blending Techniques, Inspiration, and Gear (Modern Drummer, 25 October 2018)
notes: In his own words: marched quads for three years in a competitive high-school drumline, never in a band; studied logistics and "didn't touch a pair of sticks for the better part of five years"; two years in a corporate job, then quit and practised six to eight hours a day; first show at twenty-five; the Dallas band Windwalker; filled in for Invent Animate on Texas in July's farewell tour; Polyphia needed a drummer for a video, Invent Animate's drummer passed on his name, and Clay Gober called him; two and a half years with Polyphia. Blends techniques: trap drumming, "usually used in hip-hop/electronic style music", with gospel chops and groove. Inspired by Mike Mitchell, Devon Taylor, Eric Moore and Matt Garstka, for "flow, timing, independence, creativity, and sheer chops". New Levels New Devils (12 October 2018) his first full-length with the band, tracked on a Tama Starphonic Brass snare. Gear: Tama Iron Cobra 900 Power Glides, the Meinl Matt Garstka Fat Stack.

title: Interview: Polyphia Bring the Audacity on Best Album to Date (New Noise Magazine, Nicholas Senior, 3 November 2022)
notes: Aeschliman came to the kit late: drum line in high school, then five or six years away; discovering gospel drummers moved him away from double bass. On Remember That You Will Die he heard half the material before the studio for the first time, and wrote some parts as MIDI on a computer, which let him make trap beats unlike his usual playing. He wrote The Audacity's drum solo in a day alone in the studio; the record has his second, toned-down version.

title: Meinl Cymbals - 16 Questions w/ Clay Aeschliman from Polyphia (YouTube, at85tXCgv9A)
notes: Read from the video's captions. First learned metalcore (August Burns Red's whole discography, Asking Alexandria, A Skylit Drive); stage fright for his first five years in Polyphia; most-used rudiment besides the double stroke roll the paradiddle-diddle, orchestrated round the kit; his favourite fill "a split paradiddle diddle between your hand and your foot"; the drum solo of The Audacity his craziest fill; Tim Henson's small, dry drum room makes the drums sound "more like electronic style trap style drums"; favourite drum corps the Blue Devils of 2005-2008 and Tim Jackson, "greatest quad player of all time"; his style "trap style progressive rock metal".

title: Meinl Cymbals - Clay Aeschliman's Setup Rundown (YouTube, fJH01yTx5M4)
notes: Read from the video's captions: the same set "for the better part of seven years": a 12" Classics Custom Dark trash stack, used "in place of like side snare auxiliary hits" in electronic music; 14" Classics Custom Dark hats; a 10" Pure Alloy splash; an 18" Dual crash; an 18" Pure Alloy medium crash; a Generation X 8"/10" electro stack, the three played off each other ("a lot of my patterns ... accenting between these two stacks off the hat"); a 21" Byzance Dark ride, never crashed; a 20" Byzance medium crash; the 18" Fat Stack (Matt Garstka Artist Concept); a 16" Classics Custom Trash China.

title: G.O.A.T. - Polyphia Drum transcription (Adam Miller, Flamscribed, June 2019)
notes: Flat.io score, 81 bars at 107, with a free PDF on Google Drive (drive.google.com/open?id=128PH1HCVSee0Bja8dWNBDCXH4X-k1sBI, read in full). Names the big and little stacks, the splash and the china; marks the kick's straight sixteenths in bars 13-14 and 45 as "probably backing track"; says the fast hat sequences at the start are "a little wrong".

title: O.D. - Polyphia Drum Transcription (Adam Miller, Flamscribed, May 2020)
notes: Flat.io score, 96 bars at 135, read from the video. Uses concert footage, the official video and Clay's Meinl playthrough, "the Meinl video of Clay as the 'official' template" where they differ; names the fat (18") stack, the mid (12" trash) stack, the lil (8"/10" electro) stack, crash, china and splash.

title: 'Playing God' drum transcription ver. (drum sound only) (Ahn's Drumstory, September 2022)
notes: A Seoul drum teacher's drums-only cover with his score of the record under it, 90 bars at 137, read from the video. A circled x for the stack, an x on a ledger line for the crash, a diamond for the ride's bell; an x on the middle line that the score does not name.
